title: Tourist Season, 2007 · the map
logline: Two days after: the tourist asks where the walk goes — the alley, the road, the post, the stairs, the log — and Wood, instead of answering, draws it on a napkin, and then keeps the napkin. It goes on the corkboard a month later as the walk map. This is where it comes from.

panels.composition: The seawall bench. The TOURIST with a map of the town open, pointing. WOOD. BARNABY.

balloons.text: Where's the walk go? The one in the strip.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a tourist on a seawall bench pointing at an open town map beside a thin man and a small dog

panels.composition: WOOD taking a napkin and a pen instead.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man drawing on a paper napkin with a pen on a bench

panels.composition: The napkin: a dotted line — alley, road, post, stairs, log — and '1999–' in the corner.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, close on a paper napkin with a hand-drawn dotted route past a few small landmarks and a date in the corner

panels.composition: WOOD folding the napkin and putting it in his own pocket. The tourist's hand still out.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man tucking a napkin into his own coat pocket while a tourist's hand stays held out

art.line: brush-pen scanned; muddy digital flats; Sundays in watercolor, improving
art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays gray-green, rust, one warm

notes: Where the walk map comes from (objects.md · corkboard, Jul 13 2007 — the date the board gets it is the Sunday's).
